description: Machine-readable inventory of error-handling audit checks for validation and generated maps.

statusTaxonomy.present: The expected invariant is fully satisfied.
statusTaxonomy.partial: Most signals resolve, with a small number of exceptions, or the codebase shows mixed adherence to a soft check.

relatedAudits.relationship: Owns the useUnknownInCatchVariables compiler flag; catch typing overlaps.
Owns secret redaction; sensitive-data logging overlaps.

checks.title: No empty catch blocks
checks.expectation: No catch with an empty body.
checks.violationSignal: Any empty catch, reported with file and line.

checks.title: No silently swallowed errors
checks.expectation: Every catch logs or reports the error, returns a typed result, or rethrows with context.
checks.violationSignal: A catch that does none of the three, reported with file and line.

checks.title: No string or non-Error throws
checks.expectation: Every throw throws an Error or subclass.
checks.violationSignal: throw of a string, number, or plain object, reported with file and line.

checks.title: TypeScript catch typing
checks.expectation: useUnknownInCatchVariables is enabled, or every catch parameter in source is annotated : unknown.
checks.violationSignal: The compiler option is off and untyped or any-typed catch parameters appear in source.

checks.title: Error chaining preserves cause
checks.expectation: When rethrowing or wrapping, the original is attached via the cause option.
checks.violationSignal: A catch whose body throws a fresh error without referencing the original.

checks.title: Domain errors use custom classes
checks.expectation: At least one custom error class hierarchy exists for domain errors.
checks.violationSignal: All thrown errors are bare Error.

checks.title: Network calls have error paths
checks.expectation: Every network call site has surrounding error handling or explicitly propagates the failure through its return type.
checks.violationSignal: An awaited fetch or axios call with no surrounding error handling and no upward propagation.

checks.title: Network calls have timeout configuration
checks.expectation: Each network primitive uses AbortSignal.timeout, a query-layer signal, or an explicit timeout option.
checks.violationSignal: Network calls without any timeout.

checks.title: Retry logic for retriable failures
checks.expectation: Retry behaviour is centralised in the data layer with explicit retriable conditions.
checks.violationSignal: Inconsistent per-call-site retries, or no retry strategy in an application that depends on network reliability.

checks.title: Status-code branching is explicit
checks.expectation: Network responses distinguish 4xx from 5xx and from network errors, not conflated into a single string.
checks.violationSignal: if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Request failed') with no status discrimination.

checks.title: Top-level async errors captured
checks.expectation: Async functions invoked from non-await contexts capture rejections explicitly.
checks.violationSignal: An async arrow passed as an event handler with no internal try/catch, or an awaited call inside useEffect with no error path.

checks.title: AbortController for cancellable requests
checks.expectation: Components that may unmount while a request is pending use AbortController or the data layer's signal to cancel on unmount.
checks.violationSignal: A bare fetch inside useEffect with no cleanup.

checks.title: Root error boundary present
checks.expectation: At least one error boundary wraps the application root.
checks.violationSignal: No root boundary detected.

checks.title: Route- or feature-level boundaries
checks.expectation: Boundaries exist at route or feature-cluster level, not only at the root.
checks.violationSignal: Only a single root boundary present in an application with multiple routes or features.

checks.title: Fallback UI offers recovery
checks.expectation: Boundary fallback components include at least one recovery affordance.
checks.violationSignal: A fallback that only renders an error message with no action.

checks.title: Boundary forwards to reporting service
checks.expectation: The boundary's error handler calls the detected error-reporting service.
checks.violationSignal: A boundary that only renders the fallback without reporting.

checks.title: Suspense paired with error boundary
checks.expectation: Every Suspense that wraps async-loaded data has an error boundary as an ancestor.
checks.violationSignal: A Suspense with no error boundary upstream.

checks.title: No try/catch around JSX render
checks.expectation: Render functions do not wrap return values in try/catch, since that does not catch render errors.
checks.violationSignal: A try/catch whose try block returns JSX.

checks.title: Mutation errors handled at call site
checks.expectation: Data-layer mutations have explicit onError handlers, or the consuming component handles isError.
checks.violationSignal: Mutations with no error handling and no consuming isError branch.

checks.title: Error-reporting service integrated
checks.expectation: A recognised error-reporting service is installed as a dependency.
checks.violationSignal: No error-reporting service detected.

checks.title: Reporting initialised at entry point
checks.expectation: Initialisation happens before any application code runs, in the entry point.
checks.violationSignal: The service is installed but not initialised in the entry point.

checks.title: Release versioning attached
checks.expectation: The reporting client is configured with a release identifier.
checks.violationSignal: No release configuration.

checks.title: Source maps uploaded
checks.expectation: A continuous-integration step uploads source maps to the reporting service after a successful build.
checks.violationSignal: No upload step detected in any workflow file.

checks.title: Production sample rate configured
checks.expectation: The reporting client has an explicit trace sample rate in production, not the SDK default.
checks.violationSignal: The default sample rate in production.

checks.title: No console.log in production code paths
checks.expectation: console.log, console.debug, and console.warn are absent from production code except when guarded by an environment check.
checks.violationSignal: Unguarded console.* calls in production source.

checks.title: Structured logging
checks.expectation: Logger calls pass a context object alongside the message, not a single string-concatenated argument.
checks.violationSignal: Logger calls that only pass a string.

checks.title: Sensitive-data redaction configured
checks.expectation: The reporting client scrubs passwords, tokens, and PII keys before send, or documents a safe-field allowlist.
checks.violationSignal: No redaction configured.

checks.title: Single log per error
checks.expectation: An error that is caught, logged, and rethrown is not logged again at every layer above.
checks.violationSignal: Patterns where the same error path logs at multiple layers.
